title: REST, SOAP, Bulk, Composite, UI, GraphQL, Metadata, and Tooling APIs

objectives: Choose REST, SOAP, Bulk (prefer 2.0), Composite, UI API, GraphQL, Metadata, or Tooling from official 'which API' guidance—not from habit.
State protocol, typical payload format, and sync vs async for each family using Trailhead/Help tables.
Separate data APIs (records) from Metadata API (org customizations) and Tooling API (dev tools).
Refuse Bulk for tiny interactive work and REST-per-row for large how-much loads (INT-001).
diagnostic_question: You must insert 50,000 LAB_Item__c rows overnight, patch one Account from a mobile screen, retrieve a page layout, and power a Lightning list view. Which API family for each, and which two would you not swap?
definition: Salesforce exposes many Platform APIs. REST API is a synchronous HTTP resource API (JSON or XML) for record and related operations. SOAP API is a synchronous WSDL/XML API. Bulk API 2.0 is an asynchronous REST API optimized for large datasets (CSV). Composite runs a series of REST requests in one POST. UI API serves Lightning-style UI data. GraphQL returns only requested fields in one JSON request. Metadata API manages customizations, not business records. Tooling API builds development tools and retrieves smaller metadata pieces. ([Which API Do I Use?](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/api_basics/api_basics_overview); [REST API](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_rest.meta/api_rest/intro_what_is_rest_api.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers fail candidates who say 'we always use REST' for a million-row load or who deploy fields with the data API. Wrong family burns API allocations, timeouts, and release safety.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of the Platform as a transit hub. REST is a city courier: one package, wait for the receipt. SOAP is a formal freight contract with a WSDL manifest. Composite is a courier who chains several stops in one trip. Bulk 2.0 is a freight train you dispatch and check later. GraphQL is a packing list that ships only the fields you ticked. UI API is the passenger information display Lightning already speaks. Metadata is the track-layout crew, not the cargo. Tooling is the workshop instruments for builders.
deeper_explanation: Official 'When to Use' guidance: REST for convenient web/mobile integration; combine with UI API when building record UI (list views, actions, dependent picklists); use Connect REST for Chatter/Experience/CMS-style resources; if many records, consider Bulk. SOAP for languages that want WSDL and XML. Bulk is REST-based and asynchronous; submit and retrieve results later. Metadata API is for retrieving/deploying customizations (sandbox to production), not the data itself. Tooling API is for custom development tools and smaller metadata retrieves. GraphQL uses field selection, aggregation, and schema introspection. ([API Basics](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/api_basics/api_basics_overview))

Bulk API 2.0 vs Bulk API: Salesforce recommends Bulk API 2.0 for a streamlined workflow, simpler limits, and future innovation. Official Bulk guide: operations of more than 2,000 records are good Bulk 2.0 candidates; fewer than 2,000 should use bulkified synchronous REST (for example Composite) or SOAP. Asynchronous Bulk has no SLA. ([Bulk API 2.0 intro](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_asynch.meta/api_asynch/asynch_api_intro.htm))

SOAP API works with sObjects. Enterprise WSDL is strongly typed and changes when your schema changes. Partner WSDL is loosely typed for multi-org clients. SOAP API requires Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, or Developer Edition. ([SOAP API](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api.meta/api/sforce_api_quickstart_intro.htm))

Composite is a REST resource that executes a series of REST API requests in a single POST (or lists composite resources with GET). Exact subrequest caps are versioned—Needs verification in the current Composite resource topic before quoting a number in an interview. Auth for all of these APIs is INT-004, not solved by picking REST.

mental_model.analogy: A transit hub: couriers, freight contracts, chained vans, freight trains, packing lists, departure boards, track crews, and workshop tools—each is an API family, not a business outcome.
useful_mapping: REST API → courier with JSON/XML envelope, wait for receipt
SOAP API → WSDL contract, XML only, wait for receipt
Composite → one trip with several REST stops
Bulk API 2.0 → freight train, come back later (CSV)
GraphQL → packing list: only ticked fields
UI API → Lightning passenger display (layouts, list views, actions)
Metadata API → rebuild the tracks (customizations), not the cargo
Tooling API → instruments in the builder workshop
sObject rows → cargo; custom object definitions → track plans
where_it_breaks: Pub/Sub API is another official data API (gRPC) owned by INT-007, not this hub map.
Apex REST/SOAP you write are custom endpoints, not the standard REST/SOAP families.
Composite is still synchronous; it is not Bulk.
Do not invent daily API allocation numbers; use Limits docs for the org.

claims.claim: REST API is a REST-based web service for interacting with Salesforce (CRUD, query/search, object metadata, limits) and supports XML and JSON. It is synchronous.
claims.validation: REST intro plus Trailhead When to Use REST API.

claims.claim: SOAP API is a synchronous SOAP/WSDL XML API. Enterprise WSDL is strongly typed to the org schema; Partner WSDL is loosely typed for multiple orgs. SOAP API requires Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, or Developer Edition.
claims.validation: SOAP API Developer Guide about SOAP API.

claims.claim: Bulk API 2.0 and Bulk API are REST-based asynchronous APIs for large data sets. Use Bulk API 2.0 instead of Bulk API when you want a streamlined workflow and future innovation. Operations over 2,000 records are good Bulk 2.0 candidates; under 2,000 should use bulkified synchronous REST (for example Composite) or SOAP. Salesforce does not guarantee an SLA for Bulk.
claims.validation: Bulk API 2.0 and Bulk API introduction.

claims.claim: Metadata API retrieves/deploys customizations (for example custom objects and page layouts), not the business data itself. Tooling API is for building development tools and can retrieve smaller metadata pieces. GraphQL returns only requested fields, can aggregate related resources, and supports schema introspection. Composite executes a series of REST requests in one POST.
claims.validation: Metadata intro, Trailhead when-to-use, REST resources list.

changed_in_release: Prefer Bulk API 2.0 over original Bulk API. Reverify Composite subrequest limits and GraphQL capabilities for API 67.0 / Summer '26.
unresolved_uncertainty: Exact Composite, composite graph, and sObject Collections subrequest maxima are versioned—Needs verification in the current REST Composite topics before quoting numbers.
Daily API request allocations are edition- and license-specific.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: I pick the API family after INT-001's how much and how fast. Interactive records: REST, SOAP, Composite, GraphQL, or UI API. Large async: Bulk 2.0. Shapes of the org: Metadata. Dev tools: Tooling. I do not load millions with REST-per-row.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: Trailhead's table gives protocol, format, and sync vs async. REST is the default convenient data API. SOAP when the client needs WSDL/XML. Composite when several related REST operations should travel together. Bulk 2.0 when the official intro's 2,000-record guidance says async bulk. UI API when building Lightning-like UI. GraphQL when the client must select fields and aggregate. Metadata never substitutes for data APIs. Auth is INT-004.

terminology.plain: HTTP resources for Salesforce data, usually JSON, and you wait for the response.
terminology.precise: A REST-based web services interface for CRUD, query/search, object metadata, and limits; supports JSON and XML; synchronous.
terminology.example: GET /services/data/v67.0/sobjects/Account/001... for a LAB_ Account in a sandbox.
terminology.non_example: A Bulk 2.0 ingest job you poll later.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Apex REST you author: custom endpoint, not the standard REST API family.
terminology.boundary: UI API and Connect REST are related REST families with different resources.

terminology.plain: XML web service described by a WSDL, still request/response.
terminology.precise: SOAP/WSDL API for create/retrieve/update/delete/search; XML only; synchronous. Enterprise WSDL is strongly typed to the org; Partner WSDL is loosely typed.
terminology.example: A Java client generated from Enterprise WSDL updating LAB_Account.
terminology.non_example: Metadata API deploy of a layout, even though Metadata also uses SOAP/WSDL.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Metadata API: customizations, not record CRUD as its purpose.
terminology.boundary: Edition gate: Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, or Developer as documented.

terminology.plain: Send a large CSV job and come back for results; do not wait in one HTTP round-trip for the whole load.
terminology.precise: Asynchronous REST API optimized for large insert/update/upsert/delete/query. Prefer 2.0 over original Bulk API. CSV for 2.0. No SLA.
terminology.non_example: Patching one Account from a mobile screen.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Composite: still synchronous chaining, not a freight-train job.
terminology.boundary: Official intro uses 2,000 records as a candidate threshold, not a hard compiler limit.

terminology.plain: Several REST calls packaged in one POST so you reduce chattiness.
terminology.precise: REST Composite resource executes a series of REST API requests in a single POST. Subrequest limits are versioned—verify current docs.
terminology.example: Create LAB_Account then LAB_Contact with a reference id in one composite POST.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: GraphQL aggregation: different protocol, similar 'fewer round trips' goal.
terminology.boundary: Do not invent allOrNone defaults without the Composite topic.

terminology.plain: The API Lightning uses to know layouts, list views, actions, and record UI data.
terminology.precise: User Interface API: REST/JSON synchronous API to build UI for CRUD including list views, actions, and dependent picklists.
terminology.example: A custom LWC that needs layout-aware fields uses UI API rather than raw sObject describe only.
terminology.non_example: Metadata API retrieve of Layout metadata for deployment.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: REST sObject resources: data without Lightning UI metadata.
terminology.boundary: LWC wire adapters often wrap UI API; that is LWC-006/007.

terminology.plain: Ask for exactly the fields and related records you need in one JSON query.
terminology.precise: Synchronous GraphQL/JSON API using field selection, resource aggregation, and schema introspection so clients avoid over-fetching and extra round trips.
terminology.example: A mobile screen querying Account name plus related Contacts in one GraphQL request.
terminology.non_example: SOQL via REST query that always returns a fixed sObject shape you did not select field-by-field in GraphQL.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Composite: REST subrequests, not a GraphQL schema.
terminology.boundary: Access still respects user permissions; introspection shows what the user can see.

terminology.plain: Move org shape—objects, layouts, fields—not the rows users type.
terminology.precise: Retrieve, deploy, create, update, or delete customization information such as custom object definitions and page layouts. Intended for managing the metadata model, not the data itself.
terminology.example: Deploy LAB_Item__c.object-meta.xml from sandbox to another sandbox.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Tooling API: smaller, tool-oriented metadata access.
terminology.boundary: Change sets and CLI deploy use this family; DevOps track owns pipelines.

terminology.plain: API for building developer tools, with SOAP or REST, often smaller metadata slices.
terminology.precise: Build custom development tools; SOQL on many metadata types for smaller retrieves and interactive tools. SOAP and REST interfaces.
terminology.example: An IDE listing Apex class symbols via Tooling API.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Metadata API full retrieve/deploy of packages.
terminology.boundary: Not a substitute for REST data CRUD.

when_to_use: When you must choose among REST, SOAP, Bulk, Composite, UI, GraphQL, Metadata, and Tooling APIs in a design review.
When how much is large enough that the Bulk 2.0 guide's 2,000-record candidate guidance applies.
When a client needs a WSDL/XML SOAP contract rather than REST JSON.
When several related REST operations should travel as one Composite POST instead of chatty calls.
When the job is org customizations (Metadata) or developer-tool metadata (Tooling), not record data.
when_not_to_use: Do not use REST-per-row as a substitute for Bulk API 2.0 on large async loads.
Do not use Metadata API to insert business records, or Tooling API as your ERP sync.
Do not treat Composite as asynchronous Bulk, or GraphQL as a Metadata deploy tool.
Do not pick SOAP for a Lightning UI without checking UI API, or invent Composite numeric caps.
Do not use this API catalog to skip OAuth/connected apps (INT-004) or the INT-001 pattern decision.

hands_on_lab.environment: Disposable sandbox; Workbench or Salesforce CLI against LAB_ data only.
steps: Call REST GET /services/data/v67.0/sobjects and confirm LAB_ or Account is listed.
Read the Bulk 2.0 intro and write one comment in a scratch Apex or README: jobs over 2,000 records prefer Bulk 2.0.
Retrieve one custom field or layout with Metadata API or `sf project retrieve` and note it is customization, not rows.
In a test class or script, do not loop 50 Http callouts; instead assert a boolean chooseBulk = recordCount > 2000.
guided_completion: If chooseBulk is false for 50,000, the threshold mapping is wrong.
If you retrieved records with Metadata API, you used the wrong family.
hands_on_lab.independent_challenge: Add a fifth job: chained Account+Contact create → label Composite and cite the Composite resource, without inventing a subrequest cap.
evidence: Written Bulk vs REST decision using the 2,000-record candidate guidance.
stop_recovery_cleanup: Do not leave Bulk jobs running unattended.
hands_on_lab.limitations: Lab does not execute a 50k Bulk ingest; it proves family choice.

decision_table.signal: Interactive CRUD or query, modest how much, JSON client.
decision_table.choose: REST API (add Composite if several related REST calls must travel together).
decision_table.not: Bulk API 2.0 for a handful of rows, or Metadata API for the rows.
decision_table.why: Trailhead: REST is convenient for web/mobile; Bulk is for large async sets.

decision_table.signal: Client requires WSDL and XML types generated from the org.
decision_table.choose: SOAP API with Enterprise WSDL (or Partner WSDL for multi-org).
decision_table.not: GraphQL or UI API as a WSDL substitute.
decision_table.why: SOAP API is the official WSDL/XML synchronous data API.

decision_table.signal: Insert/update/query many thousands of records asynchronously.
decision_table.choose: Bulk API 2.0 (not original Bulk API unless you have a documented reason).
decision_table.not: Synchronous REST or SOAP per row.
decision_table.why: Official Bulk intro: >2,000 records are good Bulk 2.0 candidates; no SLA.

decision_table.signal: Build Lightning-like record UI: layouts, list views, actions, dependent picklists.
decision_table.not: Metadata API retrieve of Layout as a runtime UI API.
decision_table.why: Trailhead When to Use User Interface API.

decision_table.signal: Client must select fields and related resources in one JSON request.
decision_table.not: Chatty REST without considering GraphQL or Composite.
decision_table.why: Official GraphQL benefits: field selection, aggregation, introspection.

decision_table.signal: Deploy or retrieve custom objects, fields, layouts as metadata.
decision_table.not: REST sObject CRUD or Tooling as a full org-deploy stand-in without checking the job.
decision_table.why: Metadata API is for the metadata model, not business data.

decision_table.signal: You are building an IDE or interactive metadata tool needing smaller retrieves.
decision_table.why: Trailhead When to Use Tooling API.

limitations: Composite numeric caps need current REST docs.
security_notes: Every family still uses OAuth/connected apps or equivalent (INT-004).
Tooling and Metadata widen admin surface; least privilege.

troubleshooting.symptom: Interactive API times out on a large payload.
troubleshooting.do_not_assume: JSON is always faster than SOAP.

check: You may have deployed Metadata without a data load.

production_notes: Prefer Bulk 2.0 for new large jobs.
No production loads from this lesson.

interview_questions.question: How do you choose among REST, SOAP, Bulk, Composite, UI, GraphQL, Metadata, and Tooling APIs?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: After INT-001 how much/how fast: interactive data → REST/SOAP/Composite/GraphQL/UI; large async → Bulk 2.0; org shape → Metadata; IDEs → Tooling.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I use the official when-to-use paragraphs. REST is the convenient default data API. SOAP when WSDL/XML is required. Composite to chain REST. Bulk 2.0 above the intro's 2,000-record candidate guidance. UI API for Lightning-like UI. GraphQL for field selection. I never deploy fields with REST or load rows with Metadata API. I will not invent Composite caps.
interview_questions.example: 50k nightly items → Bulk 2.0; one mobile PATCH → REST; layout deploy → Metadata.

interview_questions.question: What is different about Metadata API versus the data APIs?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Metadata API moves customizations—objects, layouts, fields. REST/SOAP/Bulk/GraphQL move or query business records. Mixing them is a classic interview fail.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Trailhead says Metadata is for managing the metadata model, not the data itself. Tooling is a neighboring metadata-oriented API for tools with smaller retrieves. A retrieve/deploy succeeding with no new Account rows is expected.
interview_questions.example: Deploy LAB_Item__c fields, then separately Bulk-load LAB_Item__c rows.

interview_questions.question: Mobile app needs Account plus Contacts with minimal payload. REST query vs GraphQL vs Composite?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: GraphQL is built for field selection and aggregating related resources in one JSON request. REST query or Composite can work but may over-fetch or need multiple subrequests.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I would not pick Bulk. I would not pick Metadata. If the UI is Lightning-like, UI API may already bundle what Lightning needs. I state GraphQL advantages from Trailhead without inventing resolver internals.
interview_questions.example: Mobile home screen: Account.Name + Contacts.Name only.

interview_questions.question: Java middleware already has SOAP stubs. New requirement is 200,000-row nightly upsert. Stay on SOAP?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: No for the volume. Official Bulk guidance: large sets are async Bulk 2.0. SOAP is for real-time few-at-a-time; hundreds of thousands make SOAP less practical.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Trailhead When to Use Bulk contrasts SOAP's real-time few records with Bulk's thousands to millions. I keep SOAP for the interactive exceptions if needed. Auth still OAuth. I will not promise a Bulk SLA.
interview_questions.example: Keep SOAP getServerTimestamp-style pings; move ingest to Bulk 2.0 CSV.

interview_questions.question: Composite POST returns an error after several subrequests. What do you not assume?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I do not assume it behaved like Bulk, and I do not quote a subrequest cap from memory. I open the current Composite resource docs for allOrNone and limits.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Composite is synchronous chaining. If volume grew, the real fix may be Bulk 2.0. I check auth (401) vs limit (403 REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED) in INT-005. I reproduce in sandbox with LAB_ data.
interview_questions.example: Parent-child create where child reference id was wrong.
weak_answer_warnings: Inventing a 25-subrequest rule without the current page

interview_questions.question: A Bulk 2.0 job sits incomplete. Stakeholder wants an SLA.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I will not invent one. The Bulk introduction says Salesforce does not guarantee an SLA because processing is asynchronous.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I check job state APIs, row errors, and concurrency with other jobs. If they needed user-blocking, they chose the wrong family (INT-001 how fast). I look at Limits, not at switching to REST-per-row.
interview_questions.example: Weekend 2M-row ingest overlapping another Bulk query.

interview_questions.question: When is Tooling API the right choice over Metadata API?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When building development tools that need smaller, interactive metadata retrieves. Metadata API is the retrieve/deploy customization pipe.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Trailhead: Tooling's SOQL for many metadata types improves performance for interactive tools. I would not Tooling-sync ERP. I mention REST or SOAP interfaces exist.
interview_questions.example: A VS Code-like extension listing Apex class symbols through Tooling API in a sandbox.
follow_ups: Can Tooling deploy a full org?

interview_questions.question: Teach the transit-hub analogy and where it breaks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: REST courier, SOAP contract, Composite chained van, Bulk train, GraphQL packing list, UI departure board, Metadata track crew, Tooling workshop. It breaks for Pub/Sub and for invented limit numbers.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I map each family, then say Apex REST is a custom station you built, Composite is still waiting at the dock, and Bulk has no timetable SLA. Auth tokens are passport control in INT-004, not a train type, and I will not invent Composite subrequest caps.
interview_questions.example: On a whiteboard, map eight jobs—mobile PATCH, 50k ingest, layout deploy, LWC list view, WSDL client, chained Account-Contact, field-selected mobile query, IDE symbol list—to REST, Bulk 2.0, Metadata, UI API, SOAP, Composite, GraphQL, and Tooling.
